items.title: Determinant-line holonomy for a global anomaly test
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current batch-41 local-anomaly Definition inspected and used only to distinguish its infinitesimal class from determinant-line holonomy. Its Step 1 readiness record is missing; effective dependency level recomputed as 4 from the current supplier graph.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice: every countable family of nonempty sets admits a choice function. Fix an even integer $d\ge2$ and a compact smooth oriented Riemannian $d$-manifold $M$ without boundary. Use the negative-square real Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}_{0,d}$, generated by $\mathbb R^d$ with $vw+wv=-2\langle v,w\rangle$. The group $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$ is its subgroup generated by even products of unit vectors; its standard double cover acts by $v\mapsto svs^{-1}$ on $\mathbb R^d$ and has kernel $\{1,-1\}$. These are the Spin and covering conventions of the given-Spin-structure supplier. A smooth principal right $G$-bundle has a free, fiberwise transitive smooth right action and equivariant local trivializations by diffeomorphisms to $U\times G$; $G$ is a finite-dimensional real Lie group. A connection is a supplied smooth right-invariant horizontal complement $H$ to $\ker d\pi$ in the tangent bundle of its total space. Let $F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(M)$ be its principal right $\mathrm{SO}(d)$-bundle of positively oriented orthonormal frames. A specified spin structure is a principal right $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$-bundle $Q\to M$ with a smooth equivariant double-cover map $\lambda:Q\to F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(M)$ covering the standard double covering $\rho:\operatorname{Spin}(d)\to\mathrm{SO}(d)$. The Levi-Civita connection lifts to a connection on $Q$. Fix an irreducible complex Clifford representation on a Hermitian space $\Delta$ of dimension $2^{d/2}$, with skew-Hermitian vector action $c_\Delta$. Put $\Gamma=i^{d/2}c_\Delta(e_1)\cdots c_\Delta(e_d)$ in a positively oriented orthonormal basis and $\Delta^\pm=\ker(\Gamma\mp I)$. The restrictions of the even Clifford action to these eigenspaces are the half-spin representations $\rho_\pm$ of $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$. Define $S^\pm=Q\times_{\rho_\pm}\Delta^\pm$. Let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $G$-bundle with connection $A$, let $V_R$ be a finite-dimensional Hermitian complex vector space, and let $R:G\to U(V_R)$ be a smooth group homomorphism. Set $E_R=P\times_R V_R=(P\times V_R)/G$ for the right action $(p,v)g=(pg,R(g)^{-1}v)$, so $[pg,v]=[p,R(g)v]$. The associated-bundle and covariant-derivative supplier supplies its smooth complex bundle charts (using the underlying real representation for the real associated-bundle definition). In a smooth local section $s$ of $P$, write $A_s=s^*\omega$, where $\omega$ is the principal connection form of $H$, and define the induced connection by $\nabla^A\psi=d\psi+(dR)_e(A_s)\psi$. The supplier proves that this formula patches with the stated quotient convention under Countable Choice. Since $R$ is unitary, the fiber metric $\langle[p,v],[p,w]\rangle=\langle v,w\rangle_{V_R}$ is well-defined and this connection preserves it. Let $c:TM\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(S^+\oplus S^-)$ be the skew-Hermitian Clifford action, with $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2g(v,w)$ for $v,w\in T_xM$, and let $\nabla$ be the tensor-product connection induced by the lifted Levi-Civita connection and $A$. The chiral Dirac operator is the extension to the stated Sobolev spaces of the first-order expression in any positively oriented local orthonormal frame $(e_i)$; this expression is independent of that frame.

$$D^+_{A,R}:H^1(M;S^+\otimes E_R)\longrightarrow L^2(M;S^-\otimes E_R),\qquad D^+_{A,R}\psi=\sum_{i=1}^{d} c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}\psi\quad(\psi\in C^\infty(M;S^+\otimes E_R)),$$

where $L^2$ is the completion for the bundle metric and Riemannian volume, and $H^1$ is the completion of smooth sections in the norm $\|\psi\|_{H^1}^2=\|\psi\|_2^2+\|\nabla\psi\|_2^2$. These are complex Hilbert spaces. The smooth first-order expression is bounded from $H^1$ to $L^2$. Assume it is Fredholm in the bounded Banach-space sense: its range is closed and its kernel and quotient cokernel $L^2(M;S^-\otimes E_R)/\operatorname{ran}D^+_{A,R}$ are finite dimensional. Its index is their complex dimension difference. Its inverse determinant line is

$$\mathcal L_A=\left(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+_{A,R}\right)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+_{A,R},$$

Here $\det_{\mathbb C}W=\bigwedge^{\dim_{\mathbb C}W}_{\mathbb C}W$, including $\det0=\mathbb C$. Our phrase **inverse determinant line** means the dual of $\Delta_A=\det\ker D^+\otimes(\det\operatorname{coker}D^+)^*$; the displayed $\mathcal L$ is the line called $\mathrm{Det}$, not $\mathrm{Det}^{-1}$, in Dai–Freed §2. This explicit formula fixes the convention throughout.

The named regularized geometry means the following supplied **admissible analytic data**, rather than an arbitrary Hermitian line relabeled by a name. Test smooth dependence on each finite-dimensional smooth parameter manifold $T$ of connections on the fixed $M,P,R$. Write $\mathscr H^\pm=T\times L^2(M;S^\pm\otimes E_R)$ with common first-Sobolev domains. Supply unitary parameter connections $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ on these Hilbert bundles, preserving smooth sections and the Sobolev domains; for the fixed product identification one may take the ordinary derivative in $T$. Fix a positive inverse-length scale $\mu$ and put $\mathscr D=D^+/\mu$, with Hilbert adjoint $\mathscr D^*$. These choices and the local-counterterm convention are fixed before phases are compared.

Require $Q^+=\mathscr D^*\mathscr D$ and $Q^-=\mathscr D\mathscr D^*$ to have the supplied nonnegative self-adjoint realizations with discrete spectrum, finite multiplicities and smooth eigensections, and the same positive spectrum with multiplicity. A spectral cut is a number $a>0$ not in either spectrum on an open parameter patch $U_a\subseteq T$. The orthogonal projections onto eigenvalues $\lambda<a$, including zero modes, must form smooth finite-rank bundles $V_a^\pm\subset\mathscr H^\pm$; their complements are denoted $\mathscr H^\pm_{>a}$. The finite cut line is $L_a=(\det V_a^+)^*\otimes\det V_a^-$. For $a<b$, the operator $\mathscr D$ is invertible between the eigenbundles $V_{(a,b)}^+$ and $V_{(a,b)}^-$. Glue $L_a$ to $L_b$ by tensoring with its top exterior power $\det\mathscr D_{(a,b)}$. Finite-dimensional cancellation of these invertible modes identifies each fiber with the displayed kernel/cokernel line, even where kernel dimensions jump. Tensor factors are kept in increasing cut order; parity is $\operatorname{ind}D^+\bmod2$ if graded lines are used.

For each cut, define the scalar function $\zeta_a(z)=\sum_{\lambda>a}\lambda^{-z}$ using the positive $Q^+$ eigenvalues with multiplicity and real $\log\lambda$. Admissibility requires convergence on an initial right half-plane, a specified meromorphic continuation to a connected domain reaching $z=0$, regularity there, and smooth parameter dependence of $\zeta'_a(0)$. The **Quillen squared norm** is $\|\ell\|_Q^2=\exp(-\zeta'_a(0))\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$. Finite bands satisfy $\zeta_a-\zeta_b=\sum_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda^{-z}$ and $\|\ell_b\|_{L^2}^2=(\prod_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda)\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$, which give cut independence of this norm. No existence of that continuation for an arbitrary Fredholm family is inferred.

Project $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ to the cut subbundles and their complements. They induce a connection $\nabla^a$ on $L_a$. On the invertible complement let $\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D_{>a}=\widetilde\nabla^-_{>a}\mathscr D_{>a}-\mathscr D_{>a}\widetilde\nabla^+_{>a}$. For $t>0$ define the complex one-form $h_a(t)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathscr H^+_{>a}}(\mathscr D_{>a}^{-1}(\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D_{>a})e^{-tQ^+_{>a}})$; the trace is the absolutely convergent sum of diagonal matrix coefficients in an orthonormal eigenbasis, independent of choices within each eigenspace. Require this convergence and the smooth coefficient expansion $h_a(t)=\sum_{j=-d/2}^{-1}b_jt^j+b_0+b_{\log}\log t+o(1)$ as dimensionless $t\downarrow0$. The finite-part convention is $\operatorname{FP}h_a=b_0+\gamma_1b_{\log}$, where $\gamma_1=\int_0^\infty e^{-r}\log r\,dr=\Gamma'(1)$; the equality names the usual gamma-function derivative and fixes the log-term subtraction. The **Bismut–Freed connection** in this convention is the local formula $\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}=\nabla^a+\operatorname{FP}h_a$, as in Dai–Freed (3.6)–(3.7).

Admissibility further requires that these forms are smooth, intertwine the specified cut transitions, and are compatible with the Quillen norm: $d\|s\|_Q^2=\langle\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}s,s\rangle_Q+\langle s,\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}s\rangle_Q$ for every local section $s$. Thus in a unit frame the connection form is purely imaginary. Gauge identifications must intertwine all cut data, preserve this norm and preserve the connection after the corresponding parameter pullback. These are explicit mathematical conditions on the supplied regularization. Cut gluing reduces on a finite band to the determinant derivative $(\det\mathscr D)^{-1}\nabla(\det\mathscr D)=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathscr D^{-1}\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D)$ with the induced finite-dimensional connections; analytic existence, smooth heat expansions and naturality for all geometric families are not asserted here. In particular a Hermitian line alone does not supply this connection. Parallel transport means the solution of $\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}_{\dot A_t}s(t)=0$ with a specified initial value; in a unit frame with connection $i\beta$, it is multiplication by $\exp(-i\int\beta)$.

When the supplied real or pseudoreal fermion structure instead yields a skew-Fredholm quadratic form, include its actual **Pfaffian data**. Concretely, on a common dense Sobolev domain $W^1$ of a complex Hilbert space $W^0$, supply a bounded linear Fredholm map $B:W^1\to(W^0)^*$ such that $b(w,z)=(Bw)(z)$ is complex bilinear and skew on $W^1\times W^1$, with $\operatorname{coker}B\cong(\ker B)^*$ induced by the pairing. Supply finite spectral subspaces $W_a$ of $B^*B$ containing the kernel, with orthogonal cut bands on which $b$ is nondegenerate and no cross terms between bands. For a finite $2m$-dimensional space $W$ the Pfaffian is $\operatorname{pf}(b)=b^{\wedge m}/m!\in\det W^*$, interpreting $b\in\bigwedge^2W^*$; it is zero in odd dimension. Glue $P_a=\det W_a^*$ by the nonzero Pfaffians of the even-dimensional invertible cut bands. The resulting graded line $P$ has parity $\dim\ker B\bmod2$ and the specified natural square identification $P^{\otimes2}\cong L_B$, where $L_B$ is the displayed determinant convention applied to $B$. Its squared Quillen norm has high-mode factor $\exp(-\zeta'_{B,a}(0)/2)$, with $\zeta_{B,a}$ defined from $B^*B$ exactly as above. Its unitary connection is the one whose tensor square, under that identification, is the supplied Bismut–Freed connection of $L_B$; locally its connection form is half that determinant form in square-compatible frames. Smooth gluing, the square identification, spectral continuations, metric compatibility and gauge naturality are required Pfaffian admissibility data, not an arbitrary choice of a square root or an existence assertion for every real/pseudoreal theory.

Let $\mathcal A(P)$ be the affine space of smooth connections on $P$, and let $\mathcal G(P)$ be the group of smooth bundle automorphisms covering the identity on $M$. A gauge arrow $u:A\to A^u$ induces a unitary map $u_*:\mathcal L_A\to\mathcal L_{A^u}$ by its action on kernel and cokernel. A closed loop in background/gauge-field space consists of a smooth path $A_t$ in $\mathcal A(P)$, $0\le t\le1$, and an endpoint gauge arrow $u:A_0\to A_1$. Let $\mathrm{PT}_{A_t}:\mathcal L_{A_0}\to\mathcal L_{A_1}$ be parallel transport and $u_*:\mathcal L_{A_0}\to\mathcal L_{A_1}$ the endpoint gauge map. The closed-loop automorphism is $u_*^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}_{A_t}$ on $\mathcal L_{A_0}$. Its scalar is the holonomy $\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L)\in U(1)$. Fix the regularization and local-counterterm convention before comparing this loop phase with the infinitesimal local anomaly; the holonomy itself is additional global loop data.

items.title: Relative boundary theory and invertible anomaly inflow
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional line-duality and cancellation Definition, with the batch-41 local-anomaly interface inspected and explicitly not used to classify global holonomy. Its Step 1 readiness record is missing; effective dependency level recomputed as 5.
items.statement:
Assume the Countable Choice convention of the global-holonomy definition. For $n\ge1$ use $\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}$ with $vw+wv=-2\langle v,w\rangle$, and define $\operatorname{Spin}(n)$ as the subgroup of even products of unit vectors. Its standard cover $\rho_n(s)(v)=svs^{-1}$ is onto $SO(n)$ with kernel $\{1,-1\}$; in particular $\operatorname{Spin}(1)=\{1,-1\}$. Principal bundles and connections have the smooth right-action and horizontal-complement meaning stated in the global-holonomy definition. Fix an integer $d\ge1$. Let $Y$ be a compact oriented smooth Riemannian $(d+1)$-manifold with boundary $M=\partial Y$, oriented so that the outward unit normal followed by a positively oriented frame of $M$ gives the orientation of $Y$. Let $F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(Y)$ be the principal bundle of positively oriented orthonormal frames and choose a principal right $\operatorname{Spin}(d+1)$-bundle $Q_Y$ with a smooth equivariant double-cover map $\lambda_Y:Q_Y\to F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(Y)$ over $\operatorname{Spin}(d+1)\to\mathrm{SO}(d+1)$. This is the spin structure on $Y$; its connection is the lift of the Levi-Civita connection. On $M$, let $F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(TM)$ denote the positively oriented orthonormal frame bundle for the induced boundary metric. The frames $(\nu_{\mathrm{out}},e_1,\ldots,e_d)$ in $F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(TY)|_M$ form a reduction identified with $F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(TM)$, where $\nu_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the outward unit normal. The preimage of this reduction under $\lambda_Y$, with structure group $\jmath(\operatorname{Spin}(d))=\rho_{d+1}^{-1}(\operatorname{diag}(1,SO(d)))$, is a principal $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$-bundle $Q_M\to F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(TM)$ double-covering that frame bundle; this is the induced boundary spin structure. The embedding $\jmath$ is induced by $\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d+1}$, $(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\mapsto(0,x_1,\ldots,x_d)$, on Clifford algebras and their even unit-vector products; it intertwines $\rho_d$ with the block embedding $h\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(1,h)$. The preimage equality is verified below. Thus the subgroup fixes the first vector through its orthogonal action, rather than by the spinor representation. A background $b$ consists of these metrics and spin structures, together with any specified principal-bundle connections and associated fields on $Y$; restriction gives the boundary background $b|_M$.

A $d$-dimensional boundary theory is **relative to an invertible bulk theory** when its partition value is a vector $Z_\partial(M,b|_M)$ in a specified one-dimensional Hermitian line $\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)$, and the bulk assigns a one-dimensional Hermitian line $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)$ together with a specified unitary isomorphism $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\cong\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)^*$ and a vector $Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y,b)$ in that bulk line. The canonical evaluation

$$\mathrm{ev}:\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\longrightarrow\mathbb C$$

then defines the combined scalar amplitude. Invertibility means that the bulk assigns a one-dimensional line to each closed $d$-dimensional background and an isomorphism to each bordism map; orientation reversal replaces the assigned line by its dual. For every finite-dimensional smooth parameter manifold $T$ and smooth family of compatible boundary backgrounds over $T$, assume the boundary and bulk lines form Hermitian line bundles $\mathcal L_\partial$ and $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}$ over $T$ with specified unitary connections $\nabla^\partial$ and $\nabla^{\mathrm{bulk}}$. The unitary line-duality isomorphism above is part of the background data and is equivariant under endpoint gauge maps, but it is not assumed to preserve these connections. A loop $\gamma$ consists of a smooth path of such backgrounds and an endpoint gauge identification $u$; let $\mathrm{PT}^{\partial}_\gamma$ and $\mathrm{PT}^{\mathrm{bulk}}_\gamma$ denote parallel transport for these connections, and let $u_*^\partial$ and $u_*^{\mathrm{bulk}}$ be the induced endpoint maps on the two lines. Denote the scalars of $(u_*^\partial)^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}^{\partial}_\gamma$ and $(u_*^{\mathrm{bulk}})^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}^{\mathrm{bulk}}_\gamma$ by $\operatorname{Hol}_\gamma(\mathcal L_\partial)$ and $\operatorname{Hol}_\gamma(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}})$, respectively; they lie in $U(1)$ because the line metrics and connections are Hermitian and unitary. Its mapping torus $Y_\gamma$ has underlying manifold $M\times S^1$, with the principal-bundle and associated fields glued at the circle seam using $u$ and any specified spin clutch, and product orientation $\operatorname{or}(M)\wedge dt$. Whenever the closed bulk response on this mapping torus is used to compute the bulk-line holonomy, the convention is

$$Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y_\gamma,b_\gamma)=\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}),$$

not its inverse. This equality is part of the adopted bulk/line data. The boundary/bulk pair cancels that anomaly along $\gamma$ exactly when

$$\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_\partial)\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}})=1.$$

The diagram records this condition: the vertical maps are the line evaluation at the two endpoints, and the top map is parallel transport on both lines.

~~~tikzcd
\mathcal L_{\partial,0}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},0}
  \arrow[r,"\mathrm{PT}^{\partial}_{\gamma}\otimes\mathrm{PT}^{\mathrm{bulk}}_{\gamma}"]
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_0"'] &
\mathcal L_{\partial,1}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},1}
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_1"] \\
\mathbb C \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}"'] & \mathbb C
~~~

items.title: A global SU(2) determinant-line phase and its mod-two inflow cancellation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; the index-one equality remains an explicit source-supported hypothesis, and the batch-41 local-anomaly interface is used only to separate local scope from holonomy. Its Step 1 readiness record is missing; effective dependency level recomputed as 6.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Assume full Axiom of Choice for the analytic product-kernel and mod-two-index calculation on every index-one background below, as well as for the concrete round-sphere benchmark. The finite-dimensional inverse-determinant sign calculation itself needs no additional choice principle. Let $M=S^4$ have its boundary orientation, a specified smooth Riemannian metric, and the standard spin structure induced from the Euclidean $5$-ball. Here a spin structure means a principal right $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$-bundle $Q\to M$ with a smooth equivariant double-cover map to the principal $\mathrm{SO}(4)$-bundle $F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(M)$ of positively oriented orthonormal frames, covering $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\to\mathrm{SO}(4)$. Let $\Delta^\pm$ be the complex half-spin representations with representation maps $\rho_\pm$, and let $S^\pm=Q\times_{\rho_\pm}\Delta^\pm$ be their associated bundles; the Levi-Civita connection lifts to $Q$. Let $E\to M$ be a smooth rank-two Hermitian bundle with a specified $SU(2)$ reduction of its unitary frame bundle. Let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection compatible with that reduction, meaning that in each $SU(2)$ frame its local connection matrix is traceless anti-Hermitian, so is valued in $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. Treat $SU(2)$ as a nondynamical background global symmetry and consider the chiral Dirac family for one massless left-handed Weyl doublet in the fundamental representation. Use the Clifford convention $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2g(v,w)$ for $v,w\in T_xM$, and the tensor-product spin and gauge connection in $D_A^+=\sum_i c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}:H^1(M;S^+\otimes E)\to L^2(M;S^-\otimes E)$. Here $(e_i)$ is any positively oriented local orthonormal frame and the expression is frame-independent. The $H^1$ norm is $\|u\|_{H^1}^2=\|u\|_2^2+\|\nabla u\|_2^2$ and $L^2$ uses the bundle metric and Riemannian volume; these are complex Hilbert spaces, and the smooth first-order expression defines a bounded map between them. For complex Banach spaces $X,Y$, a bounded complex-linear map $T:X\to Y$ is Fredholm when its range is closed and both $\ker T$ and $\operatorname{coker}T:=Y/\operatorname{ran}T$ are finite dimensional; its index is $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}T:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker T-\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}T$. Put $n_+=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker D_A^+$ and $n_-=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D_A^+$. Assume this bounded chiral realization is Fredholm with $n_+-n_-=\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D_A^+=1$; this is the index-one-sector hypothesis. The chosen boundary line in this theorem is the inverse determinant line $\mathcal L_A=(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D_A^+)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D_A^+$, equipped with the supplied Quillen metric and Bismut--Freed unitary connection. This explicitly selects the complex chiral determinant line; no identification with the fermionic Pfaffian line of a pseudoreal path-integral presentation is asserted. For $N$ independent identical doublets use $\mathcal L_A^{\otimes N}$. For a proved concrete instance, assume full AC and take the unit round metric, $E=S^+$ and the positive-spin Levi-Civita connection: its complex chiral kernel has dimension $1$, its cokernel dimension $0$, and $\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-1$ in the convention $c(E)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$. The conditional conclusion below still applies to every stipulated index-one background; this concrete instance supplies that index by proof rather than as a physical postulate.

Let $\mathcal R^{TM}$ be the curvature $2$-form of the Levi-Civita connection, viewed as a skew-symmetric matrix of real $2$-forms, and fix the Chern--Weil convention

$$p_1(TM)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbb R}(\mathcal R^{TM}\wedge\mathcal R^{TM}),\qquad \widehat A(TM)=\det_{\mathbb C}^{1/2}\!\left(\frac{i\mathcal R^{TM}/(4\pi)}{\sinh(i\mathcal R^{TM}/(4\pi))}\right),$$

where the determinant and square root are formal power series with constant term $1$, so $\widehat A_4=-p_1(TM)/24$. With $F_A$ anti-Hermitian, set $\operatorname{ch}(E)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}\exp(-F_A/(2\pi i))$ and, for $k\ge0$, $\operatorname{ch}_k(E)=\frac1{k!}\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}((-F_A/(2\pi i))^k)$. The adopted degree-six index-density polynomial is $I_6=[\widehat A(TM)\operatorname{ch}(E)]_6=\operatorname{ch}_3(E)-p_1(TM)\operatorname{ch}_1(E)/24$. This is the formal Chern--Weil polynomial used in this theorem; no descent relation between it and an infinitesimal BRST variation is assumed here.

Let $z=-I\in SU(2)$ act on the fermion fibers and form the corresponding order-two loop $\gamma_z$ of the background/gauge-field groupoid. Since $z$ acts as $-1$ in the fundamental representation, its action on this fermion is the same twist as $(-1)^F$; use the fermion-parity mapping-torus convention represented by $Y_z=S^4\times S^1$ with product metric $g_{S^4}+dt^2$, product orientation $\operatorname{or}(S^4)\wedge dt$, and gauge connection pulled back from $S^4$, and periodic total spinors around $S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, meaning $\Psi(t+1)=\Psi(t)$. Equivalently, the central $z$ gauge clutch combined with an antiperiodic spin clutch gives this periodic total fermion boundary condition. A periodic spin clutch combined with the same $z$ gauge clutch instead gives antiperiodic total fermions; the two conventions must not be conflated in an eta-holonomy formula.

For this test take the candidate bulk line to be the dual of the boundary line with its specified unitary connection. Adopt the five-dimensional mod-two-index response $Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y_z,A)=(-1)^{N\operatorname{ind}_2D_{Y_z}}$, where $S=S^+\oplus S^-$, $D_4=\sum_i c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}$ is the full Dirac operator on $H^1(S^4;S\otimes E)$, $\Gamma$ acts by $+1$ on $S^+$ and $-1$ on $S^-$, and $D_{Y_z}=D_4+i\Gamma\partial_t$ on periodic $H^1$ sections over $Y_z$. The pseudoreal $\operatorname{Spin}(5)$ and $SU(2)$ structures give a specified parallel antiunitary involution $J$ with $J^2=1$ preserving this kernel; define $\operatorname{ind}_2D_{Y_z}=\dim_{\mathbb R}((\ker D_{Y_z})^J)\bmod2$, and stipulate that this closed response is the bulk-line holonomy $\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma_z}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}})$ in the mapping-torus orientation and endpoint-identification convention above. For $N\ge1$ copies the adopted polynomial $I_6$ vanishes and the boundary holonomy on this loop is $(-1)^N$; the bulk phase is also $(-1)^N$, so the combined boundary/bulk holonomy is $+1$. For the finite normalization check take $K$ to be a single-vertex ordered simplicial complex and the ordinary field groupoid $\mathcal F(K)=BC_2$, with one object and automorphism group $C_2=\{1,z\}$. The boundary line alone has no invariant scalar gauging weight when $N$ is odd, while its tensor product with the assigned bulk line, which is its dual has the normalized finite groupoid sum $1/2$. Even $N$ makes the boundary character trivial for this tested loop; this statement does not exclude other global anomalies or prove vanishing of the infinitesimal local anomaly outside the stated polynomial calculation.

items.design_state: Step 1 authored; worked application of the conditional global-anomaly test and finite BC2 normalization. It inherits the missing batch-41 Step 1 readiness input; effective dependency level recomputed as 7.
items.statement: Assume full AC and take the explicit unit round spin $S^4$ background with $E=S^+$ and its positive-spin Levi-Civita connection, one massless left-handed Weyl doublet of a nondynamical $SU(2)$ global symmetry, and the order-two central transformation $z=-I$ from the global-anomaly test. Use the inverse determinant line $\mathcal L_A=(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D_A^+)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D_A^+$; this example makes no identification with the Pfaffian line used in a pseudoreal fermion path-integral presentation. The local Hodge calculation gives complex chiral index $1$ and Chern number $-1$. Pair this boundary line with the assigned bulk line, which is its dual, adopting $(-1)^{\operatorname{ind}_2D_5}$ as the closed phase and as the bulk-line holonomy on the mapping torus with product orientation and periodic total spinors. The boundary line has character $\chi(1)=1$, $\chi(z)=-1$; the mapping-torus mod-two index is $1$, so the bulk character is $\chi^{-1}=\chi$ and the combined character is trivial. With $F_A$ anti-Hermitian, use $\operatorname{ch}(E)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}\exp(-F_A/(2\pi i))$, $p_1(TM)=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbb R}(\mathcal R^{TM}\wedge\mathcal R^{TM})$, and $\widehat A_4=-p_1(TM)/24$; the adopted index-density polynomial $I_6=[\widehat A(TM)\operatorname{ch}(E)]_6$ is zero. This algebraic characteristic-polynomial calculation alone does not assert vanishing of an infinitesimal BRST variation. For the finite normalization check take a single-vertex complex $K$ and the ordinary field groupoid $\mathcal F(K)=BC_2$, with one object and automorphism group $C_2$. The combined unit weight is arrow-invariant and its normalized groupoid sum is $1/2$. Without the bulk, the odd boundary character is not a scalar invariant weight and no such finite gauging sum is defined. For two identical copies the boundary character itself is trivial and the same normalized groupoid sum applies. This example tests only the stated loop and does not establish that even copies have no other anomalies.

items.physical_scope: This worked example uses one specified Euclidean SU(2) Weyl-doublet inverse- determinant-line model, the explicitly proved round index-one geometry, the central order-two test, and its mod-two-index bulk response. It does not identify this line with a fermionic Pfaffian line. The finite BC2 calculation is a normalization check, not a continuum discretization or a general anomaly classification.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is inherited through the explicit round-spin Hodge/Green and characteristic-form suppliers; the finite character calculation needs no additional choice.
